headline: President Trump Mandates White House Review Of Congressional Inquiries
seoTitle: Trump Orders Contractors To Clear Congressional Inquiries
metaDescription: President Trump has issued an executive order requiring federal contractors to consult the White House before responding to any inquiries from Congress.
aiSummaryBullets: President Trump issued an executive order requiring federal contractors to consult the White House before answering requests from Congress.
Companies are directed to withhold any communications that the administration deems privileged under the new mandate.
Congressional leaders have criticized the move, characterizing the order as an infringement on their oversight capabilities.
aiContextParagraph: The executive order, issued by President Trump, mandates that all federal contractors and subcontractors must coordinate with the White House prior to responding to official inquiries from Congress. The administration indicates that companies may be required to withhold documents or information that the executive branch considers privileged. This directive comes as anticipation builds regarding a potential increase in oversight requests from Democratic lawmakers. According to reports, failure to comply with these new requirements could result in the termination of existing government contracts. Congressional officials have expressed opposition to the order, stating that it undermines their constitutional authority to conduct oversight of federal activities. The move is viewed by critics as a strategy to limit transparency and control the flow of information between private entities and legislative bodies before Democrats assume a more influential position in congressional proceedings.
whyItIsViral: The directive is being widely reported by three independent media outlets, reflecting significant political interest in executive power and oversight.
